edit.description: the stale-hold lift covers merge-stage holds beside gate-stage, named and logged by the stage it lifted; the doc drops the run-scoped-default warrant the section no longer leaves it
the merge-stage lift arm, beside the gate-stage lift and provision-stage survival cases

summary: A merge-stage quarantine hold stays for the whole run, so a cherry-pick conflict against a trunk that has since moved holds an entry a fresh pick would land

per.section: Repeated identical failures — quarantine, then abort

acceptance: a merge-stage hold lifts on the same condition a gate-stage one does — the newest tip a verdict reported differing from the placing tick's — so the two stages the section now names together behave alike; a provision-stage hold is untouched, and the lift's log names the stage it lifted rather than spelling one
tests: a merge-stage quarantine is lifted once the newest reported tip differs from the tick that placed it
notes: Fork 1 of the quarantine-lifetime record, ruled fd923ef3: the section names merge beside gate now, and fork 2 ratified the inequality the code already compares, so `hold.tip === latestTip` (`src/loopSupervisor.ts:519`) is unchanged. Verified: `liftStaleGateHolds` (`:517`) skips every `hold.stage !== "gate"`, and its doc (`:504`) calls the merge default "an expiry the spec never granted it" — now granted. Gate case `tests/loopSupervisor.test.ts:1417`, provision `:1500`.
